column3: Therapeutic Application of Painless Nerve Growth Factor to Accelerate Endochondral Fracture Repair
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVECurrently there are no well-adopted FDA approved drug therapies available to accelerate fracture healing andpatients with poorly healing fractures typically require surgical intervention. The long-term goal of this project isto develop and validate an injectable biodegradable nanowire delivery platform for local and sustained releaseof nerve growth factor (NGF) to accelerate fracture healing. This grant proposal focuses on optimizing the timingdose and delivery platform for a novel painless isoform of NGF while also for the first time aiming to rigorouslydetermine the mechanism of action for NGF in bone regeneration.

column3: Supratherapeutic PTX Buttresses Reduce Locoregional Recurrence Rates Following Surgery for Soft Tissue Sarcomas
column4: NarrativeThis proposal evaluates new supratherapeutic paclitaxel-loaded buttresses for tumor bed implantation to reducelocoregional recurrence rates after resection of retroperitoneal non-GIST abdominal and pelvic sarcomas. Thecurrent standard of care is multivisceral resection and adjuvant therapies including radiotherapy single-dosehyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy and systemic chemotherapy fail to improve patient outcomes.This proposed approach has the potential to reduce tumor recurrence and extend survival via local applicationof high-dose adjuvant chemotherapeutics at the time of resection.

column3: Regulation of epithelial function using targeted nanowires
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVEIn this project multifunctional biodegradable nanowires are being designed manufactured andtested for their ability to interact with lung and nasal epithelial cells. Complexes that target anapically expressed cell adhesion molecule 1 integrin are being screened to identify nanowiresthat physiologically regulate airway epithelial function. One goal of this study is to evaluate 1integrin as a target for the ability to improve the barrier function of the lung epithelium and as anovel therapeutic for chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis a chronic disease with criticallyfew treatment options.

column3: Novel Piezoelectric Amino-acid Ultrasound Transducer to Deliver Drugs Through the Blood Brain Barrier
column4: NarrativeNeurodegenerative diseases and brain cancers are difficult to treat due to the presence of blood brain barrier(BBB) which prevents most of therapeutic drugs from penetrating the tight junctions of endothelial cells in thebrain microvasculature and accessing the brain tissues. Ultrasound (US) has been shown to be the most effectiveand safe method to induce the BBB opening facilitating the drug delivery into the brain tissue. Here we proposea novel biodegradable US transducer based on biodegradable flexible and highly piezoelectric nanofiber film ofglycine crystals embedded inside a polycaprolactone (PCL) polymeric matrix to facilitate drug delivery throughthe BBB for the treatment of brain cancers

column3: Therapeutic Application of Painless Nerve Growth Factor to Accelerate Endochondral Fracture Repair
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVECurrently there are no well-adopted FDA approved drug therapies available to accelerate fracture healing andpatients with poorly healing fractures typically require surgical intervention. The long-term goal of this project isto develop and validate an injectable biodegradable nanowire delivery platform for local and sustained releaseof nerve growth factor (NGF) to accelerate fracture healing. This grant proposal focuses on optimizing the timingdose and delivery platform for a novel painless isoform of NGF while also for the first time aiming to rigorouslydetermine the mechanism of action for NGF in bone regeneration.

column3: Novel Piezoelectric Amino-acid Ultrasound Transducer to Deliver Drugs Through the Blood Brain Barrier
column4: NarrativeNeurodegenerative diseases and brain cancers are difficult to treat due to the presence of blood brain barrier(BBB) which prevents most of therapeutic drugs from penetrating the tight junctions of endothelial cells in thebrain microvasculature and accessing the brain tissues. Ultrasound (US) has been shown to be the most effectiveand safe method to induce the BBB opening facilitating the drug delivery into the brain tissue. Here we proposea novel biodegradable US transducer based on biodegradable flexible and highly piezoelectric nanofiber film ofglycine crystals embedded inside a polycaprolactone (PCL) polymeric matrix to facilitate drug delivery throughthe BBB for the treatment of brain cancers

column3: Supratherapeutic PTX Buttresses Reduce Locoregional Recurrence Rates Following Surgery for Soft Tissue Sarcomas
column4: NarrativeThis proposal evaluates new supratherapeutic paclitaxel-loaded buttresses for tumor bed implantation to reducelocoregional recurrence rates after resection of retroperitoneal non-GIST abdominal and pelvic sarcomas. Thecurrent standard of care is multivisceral resection and adjuvant therapies including radiotherapy single-dosehyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy and systemic chemotherapy fail to improve patient outcomes.This proposed approach has the potential to reduce tumor recurrence and extend survival via local applicationof high-dose adjuvant chemotherapeutics at the time of resection.

column3: Regulation of epithelial function using targeted nanowires
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVEIn this project multifunctional biodegradable nanowires are being designed manufactured andtested for their ability to interact with lung and nasal epithelial cells. Complexes that target anapically expressed cell adhesion molecule 1 integrin are being screened to identify nanowiresthat physiologically regulate airway epithelial function. One goal of this study is to evaluate 1integrin as a target for the ability to improve the barrier function of the lung epithelium and as anovel therapeutic for chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis a chronic disease with criticallyfew treatment options.

column3: Biodegradable Synthetic Vascular Graft
column4: Public Health RelevanceMany treatments of cardiovascular disease require bypassing or replacing diseased blood vessels. Despiteconsiderable success with current procedures polymer-based engineered conduits can enable off-the-shelfavailability with sizes and properties better suited for both the pediatric and adult populations. The goal of thisproject is to design a vascular graft with active cell homing signals that can be transformed into a native artery-like tissue in situ and test the graft in an aged animal model.
